page.title: Revision: Variables and id()
page.introduction: Let's quickly revise what we learned about variables, objects, and identity in Python.

summary.text: A variable is a name that references an object in memory.
Variables store references, not the actual values.
id() returns the identity (memory address) of the object, not its value.
Two variables can have the same value but different identities.
When a variable is assigned a new value, it may start referring to a new object.

keyPoint.title: References an object.
keyPoint.description: A variable is just a name that refers to an object stored in memory.

remember.title: Variable ≠ object
remember.description: The variable holds a reference, not the actual value.

keyPoint.title: Contains value/type information.
keyPoint.description: An object stores the actual data along with its type and other internal information.

remember.title: Objects exist in memory
remember.description: Objects are created in memory and can be shared by multiple variables.

keyPoint.title: Binds a variable to an object.
keyPoint.description: Assignment makes a variable reference an object produced by an expression.

remember.title: Reference can change
remember.description: After assignment, x now refers to the object containing 20.

keyPoint.title: Represents object identity.
keyPoint.description: The id() function returns a unique identity for the object.

remember.title: Identity ≠ value
remember.description: id(x) identifies the object referenced by x, not the object's value.

keyPoint.title: Same value can have different identities.
keyPoint.description: Two variables may contain equal values while referring to different objects.

remember.title: Equality ≠ identity
remember.description: id(x) and id(y) are about object identity, while x == y compares values.

keyPoint.title: Some objects can change, some cannot.
keyPoint.description: Mutable objects can be modified after creation, while immutable objects cannot be changed in place.

remember.title: Mutable vs immutable
remember.description: Lists are mutable, while integers are immutable.

quickTips.text: Use meaningful variable names to make your code readable.
Use id() to understand how Python manages objects in memory.
Don't rely on id() for program logic; its value can change between runs.
Practice with small examples and predict the output before running the code.

finalTip.title: Quick Revision Tip
